evidence.title: Design and fabrication of microstructured PDMS surfaces for antifouling and drag reduction
evidence.abstract: Abstract Marine biofouling on ship hulls substantially increases hydrodynamic drag and operational costs. This study selects the barnacle, a sessile crustacean with strong adhesion ability, and develops polydimethylsiloxane films patterned with micro-cylinders to achieve dual-functional antifouling and drag reduction based on the barnacle larvae dimensions and hydrophobic principle. Bioassays with barnacle cyprid larvae demonstrated that the microstructured surfaces significantly inhibited settlement, achieving an antifouling rate of 59%. Rotational drag tests further revealed a maximum drag reduction of 7.2% at 100 rpm. To elucidate the physical mechanisms, computational fluid dynamics simulations using the volume of fluid model were conducted. The numerical results verified the stability of the entrapped gas-liquid interface within the microstructures and revealed a substantial reduction in near-wall turbulence intensity and shear stress, quantitatively validating the slip-effect mechanism. These combined experimental and numerical results demonstrate the potential of engineered microstructured surfaces for marine antifouling and drag reduction applications.

evidence.title: Bio-Derived Dual-Temperature Antifouling Coating Enabled by Oyster-Shell Valorization
evidence.abstract: Oyster-shell waste represents an abundant biogenic calcium carbonate resource with potential for conversion into functional marine coatings. This study investigates a waterborne acrylic coating incorporating oyster-shell powder thermally treated at 600 °C and AZO@SiO2 core–shell nanoparticles. During a 12-month natural-seawater deployment at Anping Harbor, the three coated panels showed markedly lower visible macrofouling than the uncoated controls, although localized deposits were visible, whereas uncoated controls exhibited substantially greater visible surface coverage. Adjacent uncoated structures also showed spatial differences in fouling coverage, although these field observations do not establish the underlying biological mechanisms. Under laboratory illumination of 100 W m−2, the coated surface reached an apparent temperature of 42.1 ± 1.8 °C at 90 s, compared with 31.2 ± 0.8 °C for the uncoated control, corresponding to an apparent temperature difference of +10.9 °C. Preliminary gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) measurements revealed time-dependent and spatially varying analytical signals tentatively associated with low-molecular-weight amines. The proposed volatile-amine-mediated deterrence and photothermal antifouling mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring controlled biological validation. In preliminary 28-day leaching tests, Cu, Zn, Sn, and Fe concentrations were below the corresponding instrumental detection limits under the tested conditions. The estimated material and basic processing cost was approximately US$4.50 m−2, subject to further economic validation. These findings demonstrate the potential of oyster-shell waste valorization for developing functional marine coating systems while identifying the analytical, ecological, and durability investigations required before broader practical deployment.

evidence.title: A Pure Physical Ship Antifouling Structural System Based on Geometric Space Constraints:Mechanism Hypothesis and Engineering Pre-research Scheme
evidence.abstract: Ship underwater barnacle biofouling continuously increases hull frictional resistance and raises fuel consumption of ocean-going cargo ships, while traditional copper-containing antifouling coatings face increasingly strict international marine environmental protection regulations. Existing chemical coatings, flexible thorn films and microcavity self-locking structures have engineering defects such as attachment failure, sharp rise in navigation resistance, adhesive peeling and sediment silting. This paper proposes a modular external steel structure system with streamline longitudinal high-low conical ribs and embedded micro serrations. Narrow groove cavities and point-line contact block the lateral expansion of barnacle larva base, and segmented streamline water barriers prevent organisms from forming long strip calcified shells along the heading direction. A supporting anchor directional spray system solves the problem of sediment silting and slot blockage in stagnant water ports.The complete engineering design is established in this paper: steel skeleton is externally installed by intermittent spot welding without modifying the ship base metal; homogeneous carbon steel strip triple sealing structure completely avoids seawater galvanic corrosion and gap water seepage; a multi-component navigation resistance splitting model is constructed, and two-stage drag reduction optimization plans are set to strictly control the additional frictional resistance within 10%. Four core scientific hypotheses verifiable by sea trials and CFD simulation are put forward, and a digital quantitative observation index system and full-life cycle inventory cost model are established. At present, all structural design, risk prevention and control and verification paths are fully closed. Subsequent fluid simulation, 12-month real sea panel exposure test and component fatigue corrosion test only need to be carried out. After data verification, real ship segmented pilot transformation can be carried out. This purely physical non-chemical antifouling technology is expected to become a new technical route for green drag reduction and marine antifouling on existing ocean-going vessels.

evidence.title: Assessing the vulnerability of Antarctic marine ecosystems to invasive non-native species
evidence.abstract: Invasive non-native species are a major threat to global biodiversity. For at least 15 million years coastal Antarctica has been poorly connected to nearby temperate ecosystems due to physical and physiological barriers. Yet, Antarctica is experiencing significant environmental change and becoming increasingly exposed to ship-borne human activity that crosses the physical barriers. These factors may facilitate the establishment of non-native marine species. This doctoral research adds insight into the risk of non-native marine species being transported to Antarctica via ships’ hulls and internal seawater systems, with particular focus on pathways of introduction and species found within those pathways. To begin my research, I assessed the current knowledge of non-native marine species in the Antarctic region: the physical and physiological factors that resist establishment of non-native marine species; changes to resistance under climate change; the role of legislation in limiting marine introductions; and the effect of increasing human activity on vectors and pathways of introduction. Evidence of non-native marine species was limited: up to 2019 just four marine non-native and one cryptogenic species that were likely introduced anthropogenically had been reported free-living in Antarctica or in the sub-Antarctica islands, but no established populations have been reported. An additional six species had been observed in pathways to Antarctica that are potentially at risk of becoming invasive. I estimated there may be approximately 180 vessels and 500+ voyages in Antarctic waters annually. However, these estimates are necessarily speculative because relevant data are not recorded comprehensively. In response to the scarcity of data on ship movements into the Southern Ocean, I obtained data on ship activity in the Southern Ocean from 2014-2018 inclusive and developed a ship traffic network for Antarctic-going vessels. I analysed the ship movements and conducted a spatially-explicit assessment of introduction risk for non-native marine species in all Antarctic waters. I found that vessels connect Antarctica via an extensive network of ship activity to all global regions, and especially South Atlantic and European ports. evidence.title: Molecular Basis of the Activity of SinR Protein, the Master Regulator of Biofilm Formation in Bacillus subtilis
evidence.abstract: Bacterial biofilms are complex communities of cells that are attached to a surface by an extracellular matrix. Biofilms are an increasing environmental and healthcare issue, causing problems ranging from the biofouling of ocean-going vessels, to dental plaque, infections of the urinary tract, and contamination of medical instruments such as catheters. A complete understanding of biofilm formation therefore requires knowledge of the regulatory pathways underpinning its formation so that effective intervention strategies can be determined. The master regulator that determines whether the Gram-positive model organism Bacillus subtilis switches from a free-living, planktonic lifestyle to form a biofilm is called SinR. The activity of SinR, a transcriptional regulator, is controlled by its antagonists, SinI, SlrA, and SlrR. The interaction of these four proteins forms a switch, which determines whether or not SinR can inhibit biofilm formation by its repression of a number of extracellular matrix-associated operons. To determine the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters governing the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions at the heart of this epigenetic switch, we have analyzed the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions by isothermal titration calorimetry and surface plasmon resonance. We also present the crystal structure of SinR in complex with DNA, revealing the molecular basis of base-specific DNA recognition by SinR and suggesting that the most effective means of transcriptional control occurs by the looping of promoter DNA. The structural analysis also enables predictions about how SinR activity is controlled by its interaction with its antagonists.

evidence.title: A short note on Reitlinger thermodynamic cycles
evidence.abstract: It is well known that Carnot cycle is the thermodynamic cycle which has the best thermal efficiency. However, an entire class of cycles exists that can have the same maximum efficiency: this class is that of the regenerative Reitlinger cycles. Here we discuss them.

evidence.title: Cycles of many lengths in digraphs with Meyniel-like condition
evidence.abstract: C. Thomassen (Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 42 (1981), 231-251) gave a characterization of strongly connected non-Hamiltonian digraphs of order $p\geq 3$ with minimum degree $p-1$. In this paper we give an analogous characterization of strongly connected non-Hamiltonian digraphs with Meyniel-type condition (the sum of degrees of every pair of non-adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$ at least $2p-2$). Moreover, we prove that such digraphs $D$ contain cycles of all lengths $k$, for $2\leq k\leq m$, where $m$ is the length of a longest cycle in $D$.

evidence.title: Effect of Optical Coating and Surface Treatments on Mechanical Loss in Fused Silica
evidence.abstract: We report on the mechanical loss in fused silica samples with various surface treatments and compare them with samples having an optical coating. Mild surface treatments such as washing in detergent or acetone were not found to affect the mechanical loss of flame-drawn fused silica fibers stored in air. However, mechanical contact (with steel calipers) significantly increased the loss. The application of a high-reflective optical coating of the type used for the LIGO test masses was found to greatly increase the mechanical loss of commercially polished fused silica microscope slides. We discuss the implications for the noise budget of interferometers.

evidence.title: Interaction Effect between Hull and Accommodation on Wind Drag Acting on a Container Ship
evidence.abstract: In this paper, we present our research on applying the commercial Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) code to investigate interaction effect between hull and accommodation on wind drag acting above the water hull surface of a full scale 1200 TEU container ship. With this purpose, aerodynamic performances and wind drag acting on the ship hull with and without accommodations have been computed. Analyzing the obtained CFD results, the interaction effect between hull and accommodation on aerodynamic performances and wind drag acting on the ship have been found. Various new accommodation shapes have been proposed for the original ship to reduce the interaction effect on wind drag. A drastic reduction in the interaction effect between hull and accommodation on wind drag acting on the ship has been achieved and the obtained results have been shown in this paper

evidence.title: Aerodynamic forces on high speed multi-hulled marine vehicles
evidence.abstract:
The need for high-speed high-payload craft has led to a considerable interest in
vehicles capable of bridging the gap between conventional ships and aircraft. One
such concept uses the forward motion of the craft to create aerodynamic forces on
a wing-like structure, and hence, alleviate the overall drag by reducing the wetted
area.
This research focuses on the use of suitably shaped multihull geometries to
achieve e cient aerodynamic lift for high-speed sea vessels. The problem is  rst
studied in two dimensions using a simpli ed analytical approach and CFD modeling.
The work is then extended into three dimensions and a  nal aerodynamic
model is produced for a complete hull form, including the e ects of hydrodynamic
surfaces above the water. The aerodynamic analysis demonstrates that signi cant
e ciency can be achieved through careful shaping of the side hull and cross deck,
with lift-to-drag ratios of nearly 50 for a complete aerodynamic hull con guration.
Further analysis is carried out using a hybrid vehicle stability model to determine
the e ect of such aerodynamic alleviation on a theoretical planing hull
vessel. Comparisons are made using the Savitsky planing model, and from this it
is found that the resistance can be almost halved for a  fty metre, three hundred
tonne vehicle with aerodynamic alleviation traveling at 70 knots.
A comparative study is made for the hybrid vehicle with regards to size, speed
and weight, whilst attempting to match the proportion of aerodynamic lift with
speed to a theoretical optimum. From this the likely con gurations for future
development are identi ed

(�) of ship is included in the model. Three players are considered, i.e. port administrator, ship companies (carriers),

and shippers. Interaction of these players leads to Nash equilibrium problem. The result of the model calculation indicates

that Hong Kong and Singapore port dominates container throughput in the world and the big vessel (3000 - 6000

TEU) is dominant in these ports. Conversely, the smaller port with depth less than 15 m dominated by 1000 TEU vessels.

less than 15 m such as port of Shanghai. Again, it is inline with reality. Validation of the model shows that coefficient of

determination (R2) is 0.95. It indicates the model provides good accuracy.

Narrow groove cavities and point-line contact block the lateral expansion of barnacle larva base, and segmented streamline water barriers prevent organisms from forming long strip calcified shells along the heading direction. A supporting anchor directional spray system solves the problem of sediment silting and slot blockage in stagnant water ports.The complete engineering design is established in this paper: steel skeleton is externally installed by intermittent spot welding without modifying the ship base metal; homogeneous carbon steel strip triple sealing structure completely avoids seawater galvanic corrosion and gap water seepage; a multi-component navigation resistance splitting model is constructed, and two-stage drag reduction optimization plans are set to strictly control the additional frictional resistance within 10%. Four core scientific hypotheses verifiable by sea trials and CFD simulation are put forward, and a digital quantitative observation index system and full-life cycle inventory cost model are established. At present, all structural design, risk prevention and control and verification paths are fully closed. Subsequent fluid simulation, 12-month real sea panel exposure test and component fatigue corrosion test only need to be carried out. After data verification, real ship segmented pilot transformation can be carried out. This purely physical non-chemical antifouling technology is expected to become a new technical route for green drag reduction and marine antifouling on existing ocean-going vessels.

system.value: Assessing the vulnerability of Antarctic marine ecosystems to invasive non-native species

abstract.value: Invasive non-native species are a major threat to global biodiversity. For at least 15 million years coastal Antarctica has been poorly connected to nearby temperate ecosystems due to physical and physiological barriers. Yet, Antarctica is experiencing significant environmental change and becoming increasingly exposed to ship-borne human activity that crosses the physical barriers. These factors may facilitate the establishment of non-native marine species. This doctoral research adds insight into the risk of non-native marine species being transported to Antarctica via ships’ hulls and internal seawater systems, with particular focus on pathways of introduction and species found within those pathways. To begin my research, I assessed the current knowledge of non-native marine species in the Antarctic region: the physical and physiological factors that resist establishment of non-native marine species; changes to resistance under climate change; the role of legislation in limiting marine introductions; and the effect of increasing human activity on vectors and pathways of introduction. Evidence of non-native marine species was limited: up to 2019 just four marine non-native and one cryptogenic species that were likely introduced anthropogenically had been reported free-living in Antarctica or in the sub-Antarctica islands, but no established populations have been reported. An additional six species had been observed in pathways to Antarctica that are potentially at risk of becoming invasive. I estimated there may be approximately 180 vessels and 500+ voyages in Antarctic waters annually. However, these estimates are necessarily speculative because relevant data are not recorded comprehensively. In response to the scarcity of data on ship movements into the Southern Ocean, I obtained data on ship activity in the Southern Ocean from 2014-2018 inclusive and developed a ship traffic network for Antarctic-going vessels. I analysed the ship movements and conducted a spatially-explicit assessment of introduction risk for non-native marine species in all Antarctic waters. I found that vessels connect Antarctica via an extensive network of ship activity to all global regions, and especially South Atlantic and European ports. system.value: Molecular Basis of the Activity of SinR Protein, the Master Regulator of Biofilm Formation in Bacillus subtilis

abstract.value: Bacterial biofilms are complex communities of cells that are attached to a surface by an extracellular matrix. Biofilms are an increasing environmental and healthcare issue, causing problems ranging from the biofouling of ocean-going vessels, to dental plaque, infections of the urinary tract, and contamination of medical instruments such as catheters. A complete understanding of biofilm formation therefore requires knowledge of the regulatory pathways underpinning its formation so that effective intervention strategies can be determined. The master regulator that determines whether the Gram-positive model organism Bacillus subtilis switches from a free-living, planktonic lifestyle to form a biofilm is called SinR. The activity of SinR, a transcriptional regulator, is controlled by its antagonists, SinI, SlrA, and SlrR. The interaction of these four proteins forms a switch, which determines whether or not SinR can inhibit biofilm formation by its repression of a number of extracellular matrix-associated operons. To determine the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters governing the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions at the heart of this epigenetic switch, we have analyzed the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions by isothermal titration calorimetry and surface plasmon resonance. We also present the crystal structure of SinR in complex with DNA, revealing the molecular basis of base-specific DNA recognition by SinR and suggesting that the most effective means of transcriptional control occurs by the looping of promoter DNA. The structural analysis also enables predictions about how SinR activity is controlled by its interaction with its antagonists.

system.value: Interaction Effect between Hull and Accommodation on Wind Drag Acting on a Container Ship

abstract.value: In this paper, we present our research on applying the commercial Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) code to investigate interaction effect between hull and accommodation on wind drag acting above the water hull surface of a full scale 1200 TEU container ship. With this purpose, aerodynamic performances and wind drag acting on the ship hull with and without accommodations have been computed. Analyzing the obtained CFD results, the interaction effect between hull and accommodation on aerodynamic performances and wind drag acting on the ship have been found. Various new accommodation shapes have been proposed for the original ship to reduce the interaction effect on wind drag. A drastic reduction in the interaction effect between hull and accommodation on wind drag acting on the ship has been achieved and the obtained results have been shown in this paper

system.value: Aerodynamic forces on high speed multi-hulled marine vehicles

abstract.value:
The need for high-speed high-payload craft has led to a considerable interest in
vehicles capable of bridging the gap between conventional ships and aircraft. One
such concept uses the forward motion of the craft to create aerodynamic forces on
a wing-like structure, and hence, alleviate the overall drag by reducing the wetted
area.
This research focuses on the use of suitably shaped multihull geometries to
achieve e cient aerodynamic lift for high-speed sea vessels. The problem is  rst
studied in two dimensions using a simpli ed analytical approach and CFD modeling.
The work is then extended into three dimensions and a  nal aerodynamic
model is produced for a complete hull form, including the e ects of hydrodynamic
surfaces above the water. The aerodynamic analysis demonstrates that signi cant
e ciency can be achieved through careful shaping of the side hull and cross deck,
with lift-to-drag ratios of nearly 50 for a complete aerodynamic hull con guration.
Further analysis is carried out using a hybrid vehicle stability model to determine
the e ect of such aerodynamic alleviation on a theoretical planing hull
vessel. Comparisons are made using the Savitsky planing model, and from this it
is found that the resistance can be almost halved for a  fty metre, three hundred
tonne vehicle with aerodynamic alleviation traveling at 70 knots.
A comparative study is made for the hybrid vehicle with regards to size, speed
and weight, whilst attempting to match the proportion of aerodynamic lift with
speed to a theoretical optimum. From this the likely con gurations for future
development are identi ed

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. cemetery_warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

candidates.mechanism: The same **vector-mediated transport mechanism** as in the source system, where **ship hulls and internal seawater systems act as pathways for biofouling organisms** (analogous to invasive species) to adhere, grow, and accumulate over time due to prolonged exposure in transit routes with high biological activity (e.g., South Atlantic/European ports). candidates.intervention: Install **passive fouling traps** in high-risk zones (e.g., propeller hubs, hull strakes, and seawater intake valves) to intercept and divert fouling organisms before they colonize critical surfaces. These traps would be designed with **selective adhesion surfaces** (e.g., optimized roughness or chemical gradients) to maximize capture efficiency while minimizing drag.

I found that vessels connect Antarctica via an extensive network of ship activity to all global regions, and especially South Atlantic and European ports. cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

candidates.intervention: Install modular external steel panels with **streamline longitudinal high-low conical ribs (rib height: 5–15 mm, pitch: 100–200 mm)** and **embedded micro serrations (serration depth: 0.3–0.8 mm, spacing: 1–3 mm)** on the hull and propeller bossing, using intermittent spot welding to a homogeneous carbon steel backing strip (triple-sealed to prevent galvanic corrosion).

hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Apply **modular carbon steel panels with alternating high/low conical ribs (rib angle: 12°–18° to flow, trough width: 30–50 mm)** to the **forward 60% of hull (bow to midship)** and **propeller boss cap**, with rib height graded from 20 mm (bow) to 5 mm (aft) to optimize shear gradient.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Sediment-flushing via directional anchor spray** — High-velocity, low-volume water jets targeted at rib troughs and serration gaps prevent sediment accumulation in stagnant ports, which otherwise provides a substrate for microbial fouling and barnacle larval settlement.

A hit sharing NO entity term with the candidate now needs >= 3 NON-generic mechanism terms to be mechanism art: the measured true cross-domain analog (line-pipe steel with hydrogen fracture toughness for a rail-steel candidate) shares 3 non-generic terms and survives; every measured false positive shares <= 2 and is demoted. This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).

custody_records.raw_content: Abstract Marine biofouling on ship hulls substantially increases hydrodynamic drag and operational costs. This study selects the barnacle, a sessile crustacean with strong adhesion ability, and develops polydimethylsiloxane films patterned with micro-cylinders to achieve dual-functional antifouling and drag reduction based on the barnacle larvae dimensions and hydrophobic principle. Bioassays with barnacle cyprid larvae demonstrated that the microstructured surfaces significantly inhibited settlement, achieving an antifouling rate of 59%. Rotational drag tests further revealed a maximum drag reduction of 7.2% at 100 rpm. To elucidate the physical mechanisms, computational fluid dynamics simulations using the volume of fluid model were conducted. The numerical results verified the stability of the entrapped gas-liquid interface within the microstructures and revealed a substantial reduction in near-wall turbulence intensity and shear stress, quantitatively validating the slip-effect mechanism. These combined experimental and numerical results demonstrate the potential of engineered microstructured surfaces for marine antifouling and drag reduction applications.

custody_records.raw_content: Oyster-shell waste represents an abundant biogenic calcium carbonate resource with potential for conversion into functional marine coatings. This study investigates a waterborne acrylic coating incorporating oyster-shell powder thermally treated at 600 °C and AZO@SiO2 core–shell nanoparticles. During a 12-month natural-seawater deployment at Anping Harbor, the three coated panels showed markedly lower visible macrofouling than the uncoated controls, although localized deposits were visible, whereas uncoated controls exhibited substantially greater visible surface coverage. Adjacent uncoated structures also showed spatial differences in fouling coverage, although these field observations do not establish the underlying biological mechanisms. Under laboratory illumination of 100 W m−2, the coated surface reached an apparent temperature of 42.1 ± 1.8 °C at 90 s, compared with 31.2 ± 0.8 °C for the uncoated control, corresponding to an apparent temperature difference of +10.9 °C. Preliminary gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) measurements revealed time-dependent and spatially varying analytical signals tentatively associated with low-molecular-weight amines. The proposed volatile-amine-mediated deterrence and photothermal antifouling mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring controlled biological validation. In preliminary 28-day leaching tests, Cu, Zn, Sn, and Fe concentrations were below the corresponding instrumental detection limits under the tested conditions. The estimated material and basic processing cost was approximately US$4.50 m−2, subject to further economic validation. These findings demonstrate the potential of oyster-shell waste valorization for developing functional marine coating systems while identifying the analytical, ecological, and durability investigations required before broader practical deployment.

custody_records.raw_content: Ship underwater barnacle biofouling continuously increases hull frictional resistance and raises fuel consumption of ocean-going cargo ships, while traditional copper-containing antifouling coatings face increasingly strict international marine environmental protection regulations. Existing chemical coatings, flexible thorn films and microcavity self-locking structures have engineering defects such as attachment failure, sharp rise in navigation resistance, adhesive peeling and sediment silting. This paper proposes a modular external steel structure system with streamline longitudinal high-low conical ribs and embedded micro serrations. Narrow groove cavities and point-line contact block the lateral expansion of barnacle larva base, and segmented streamline water barriers prevent organisms from forming long strip calcified shells along the heading direction. A supporting anchor directional spray system solves the problem of sediment silting and slot blockage in stagnant water ports.The complete engineering design is established in this paper: steel skeleton is externally installed by intermittent spot welding without modifying the ship base metal; homogeneous carbon steel strip triple sealing structure completely avoids seawater galvanic corrosion and gap water seepage; a multi-component navigation resistance splitting model is constructed, and two-stage drag reduction optimization plans are set to strictly control the additional frictional resistance within 10%. Four core scientific hypotheses verifiable by sea trials and CFD simulation are put forward, and a digital quantitative observation index system and full-life cycle inventory cost model are established. At present, all structural design, risk prevention and control and verification paths are fully closed. Subsequent fluid simulation, 12-month real sea panel exposure test and component fatigue corrosion test only need to be carried out. After data verification, real ship segmented pilot transformation can be carried out. This purely physical non-chemical antifouling technology is expected to become a new technical route for green drag reduction and marine antifouling on existing ocean-going vessels.

custody_records.raw_content: Invasive non-native species are a major threat to global biodiversity. For at least 15 million years coastal Antarctica has been poorly connected to nearby temperate ecosystems due to physical and physiological barriers. Yet, Antarctica is experiencing significant environmental change and becoming increasingly exposed to ship-borne human activity that crosses the physical barriers. These factors may facilitate the establishment of non-native marine species. This doctoral research adds insight into the risk of non-native marine species being transported to Antarctica via ships’ hulls and internal seawater systems, with particular focus on pathways of introduction and species found within those pathways. To begin my research, I assessed the current knowledge of non-native marine species in the Antarctic region: the physical and physiological factors that resist establishment of non-native marine species; changes to resistance under climate change; the role of legislation in limiting marine introductions; and the effect of increasing human activity on vectors and pathways of introduction. Evidence of non-native marine species was limited: up to 2019 just four marine non-native and one cryptogenic species that were likely introduced anthropogenically had been reported free-living in Antarctica or in the sub-Antarctica islands, but no established populations have been reported. An additional six species had been observed in pathways to Antarctica that are potentially at risk of becoming invasive. I estimated there may be approximately 180 vessels and 500+ voyages in Antarctic waters annually. However, these estimates are necessarily speculative because relevant data are not recorded comprehensively. In response to the scarcity of data on ship movements into the Southern Ocean, I obtained data on ship activity in the Southern Ocean from 2014-2018 inclusive and developed a ship traffic network for Antarctic-going vessels. I analysed the ship movements and conducted a spatially-explicit assessment of introduction risk for non-native marine species in all Antarctic waters. custody_records.raw_content: Bacterial biofilms are complex communities of cells that are attached to a surface by an extracellular matrix. Biofilms are an increasing environmental and healthcare issue, causing problems ranging from the biofouling of ocean-going vessels, to dental plaque, infections of the urinary tract, and contamination of medical instruments such as catheters. A complete understanding of biofilm formation therefore requires knowledge of the regulatory pathways underpinning its formation so that effective intervention strategies can be determined. The master regulator that determines whether the Gram-positive model organism Bacillus subtilis switches from a free-living, planktonic lifestyle to form a biofilm is called SinR. The activity of SinR, a transcriptional regulator, is controlled by its antagonists, SinI, SlrA, and SlrR. The interaction of these four proteins forms a switch, which determines whether or not SinR can inhibit biofilm formation by its repression of a number of extracellular matrix-associated operons. To determine the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters governing the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions at the heart of this epigenetic switch, we have analyzed the protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions by isothermal titration calorimetry and surface plasmon resonance. We also present the crystal structure of SinR in complex with DNA, revealing the molecular basis of base-specific DNA recognition by SinR and suggesting that the most effective means of transcriptional control occurs by the looping of promoter DNA. The structural analysis also enables predictions about how SinR activity is controlled by its interaction with its antagonists.

custody_records.raw_content: We report on the mechanical loss in fused silica samples with various surface treatments and compare them with samples having an optical coating. Mild surface treatments such as washing in detergent or acetone were not found to affect the mechanical loss of flame-drawn fused silica fibers stored in air. However, mechanical contact (with steel calipers) significantly increased the loss. The application of a high-reflective optical coating of the type used for the LIGO test masses was found to greatly increase the mechanical loss of commercially polished fused silica microscope slides. We discuss the implications for the noise budget of interferometers.

vehicles capable of bridging the gap between conventional ships and aircraft. One
such concept uses the forward motion of the craft to create aerodynamic forces on
a wing-like structure, and hence, alleviate the overall drag by reducing the wetted
area.

achieve e cient aerodynamic lift for high-speed sea vessels. The problem is  rst

surfaces above the water. The aerodynamic analysis demonstrates that signi cant
e ciency can be achieved through careful shaping of the side hull and cross deck,
with lift-to-drag ratios of nearly 50 for a complete aerodynamic hull con guration.

vessel. Comparisons are made using the Savitsky planing model, and from this it

tonne vehicle with aerodynamic alleviation traveling at 70 knots.

and weight, whilst attempting to match the proportion of aerodynamic lift with
speed to a theoretical optimum. From this the likely con gurations for future
development are identi ed
